semantic_fragments.content: The risk management process will be conducted in accordance with standard ISO 14971:2019, EN ISO 14971:2019 and EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021.

Risk Management Activities by Phase:

1. Initial development: (1) Document intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; (2) Identify characteristics related to safety; (3) Identify hazards and hazardous situations; (4) Estimate the risk(s) of each hazardous situation; (5) Risk evaluation; (6) Draft the risk control measures plan. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Report of risk assessment.

2. Prototype phase (Design verification): (1) Verify implementation and effectiveness of risk control measures plan; (2) Assess residual risk; (3) Make benefit-risk analysis; (4) Evaluate whether there are any risks arising from risk control measures; (5) Review completeness of risk control. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation.

3. Design validation: (1) Overall residual risk evaluation; (2) Form the risk management report. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Report of risk management.

4. Design change: (1) Identify hazards and hazardous situations related to design change; (2) Evaluate risk(s) in hazardous situation resulting from design change; (3) Assess risk(s) in design change; (4) Draft the plan of risk control measures for design change; (5) Verify the implementation of plan on risk control measures after design change; (6) Assess residual risk, benefit-risk analysis and any new risks after design change; (7) Overall residual risk evaluation after design change. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Record of risk evaluation (when no new risk); Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation in design change; Report of Risk Management in design change.

5. Production and post-production activities: (1) Collect information concerning production and post-production; (2) Assess if there are hazards or hazardous situations not identified before, and if the risk(s) become not acceptable; whether the overall residual risk is still acceptable in relation to the benefits of the intended use; and whether the generally acknowledged state of the art has changed; (3) Analyze and assess the risk(s) and make risk control plan and actions if necessary; (4) Track the implementation of risk control measures. Reference: Section 4.11.1 of Risk Management Control Regulation (QI-7.3-22). Output: Report of Post-market Risk Management.

Risk Management Group composition: The specific personnel may vary from different projects, but the risk assessment team generally includes the following members:
- Technical Director: Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than three years work experience.
- Product manager: Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than three years design experience.
- Project manager: Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience.
- Hardware design director: Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience.
- Software design director: Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience.

Document table of contents references the following sections which are present in the full document but may not be fully captured in this fragment:
3. Risk Acceptance Criteria (3.1 Severity of A Hazard, 3.2 Probability of A Hazard, 3.3 Risk Acceptance Criteria)
4. Residual Risk Acceptance Criteria (4.1 For Single Residual Risk, 4.2 For Overall Residual Risk)
5. Risk Control Measures Verification Criteria

Severity Classification: Catastrophic (S=5): Result in patient death; Critical (S=4): Result in permanent impairment or life-threatening injury; Serious (S=3): Result in injury or impairment requiring professional medical intervention; Minor (S=2): Result in temporary injury or impairment not requiring professional medical intervention; Negligible (S=1): Inconvenience or temporary discomfort.

Semiquantitative Probability Classification: Frequent (P=6): ≥10^-3; Probable (P=5): <10^-3 ≥10^-4; Occasional (P=4): <10^-4 ≥10^-5; Remote (P=3): <10^-5 ≥10^-6; Improbable (P=2): <10^-6 ≥10^-8; Few (P=1): <10^-8.

Risk Acceptance Criteria matrix (S×P): Not acceptable: Unacceptable risk, risk control measures are required. Control as much as possible: The risk needs to be controlled by control measures. Acceptable: Insignificant/negligible risk, no risk control measures are required. The manufacturer shall reduce the risk as far as possible using one or more of the following risk control options in priority order: (a) eliminate or reduce risks through safe design and manufacture; (b) take adequate protection measures including alarms if necessary for risks that cannot be eliminated; (c) provide information for safety (warnings/precautions/contra-indications) and training to users.

Residual Risk Acceptance Criteria - Single Residual Risk: When a risk falls in the 'Not acceptable' area, risk control measures must be taken. After taking measures, if the residual risk still falls in the 'Not acceptable' area, a risk-benefit analysis must be taken. The residual risk will be acceptable when there are reasonable reasons to support that benefits outweigh the risks.

Residual Risk Acceptance Criteria - Overall Residual Risk: (1) Benefits related to intended use are weighed against overall residual risk, considering magnitude, probability, duration and frequency of benefit, intended medical indication, state of the art, and availability of alternatives. (2) Visual representations using risk matrix can be useful; if more than 1/2 of the risks are in higher severity or probability regions, or clusters are borderline, overall residual risk might not be acceptable even if each individual risk was judged acceptable. (3) Overall risk-benefit analysis: when benefits outweigh overall residual risks, overall residual risks are acceptable. (4) If overall residual risks are acceptable, significant residual risks shall be notified to users in accompanying documents. If not acceptable, additional risk control measures shall be taken or modification to the medical device may be required.

Risk Control Measures Verification Criteria: Risk control measures of initial risks and residual risks are verified in accordance with the document Verification in Design and Development Control Procedure.

Personnel qualification requirements: Mechanical design director - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Hardware design personnel - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Software design personnel - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Mechanical design personnel - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Process design personnel - Electrics or mechanics or other related engineering specialities, more than one year design experience. Quality management personnel - Electrics or mechanics or other related engineering specialities, more than one year design experience. Sales personnel - No special requirement, familiar with handling of customer complaints process. Certification personnel - Biomedicine or mechano-electronic or other related specialities, more than two years work experience. Personnel with medical background - Biology or clinical medicine or other medical related specialities, more than three years clinical experience.
